primitives.name: Team Strength Evolution
primitives.verbatim_quote: Team strength \(\theta_{i,s,w}\) (franchise \(i\), season \(s\), week \(w\)) follows nested AR(1) evolution: between-season shock \(\sigma^2_B\), within-season week shock \(\sigma^2_W\), and game-level observation noise \(\sigma^2_G\), plus home advantage (they compare a constant-HA model vs team-specific HA).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\theta_{i,s,w}': 'Team strength, dimensionless', '\\sigma^2_B': 'Between-season variance, dimensionless squared', '\\sigma^2_W': 'Within-season weekly variance, dimensionless squared', '\\sigma^2_G': 'Game-level noise, dimensionless squared'}
primitives.assumptions: Nested autoregressive structure assumes temporal correlation in team strength, with shocks independent across levels.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \(\sigma^2_B \to 0\), implies no inter-season variability; when \(\sigma^2_W \to 0\), implies no intra-season fluctuation.

layer2.mapping: Models team latent talent dynamics through hierarchical variance components, enabling probabilistic inference on skill versus luck.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior standard deviation of \(\theta\) over time.

primitives.name: Betting Market Calibration
primitives.verbatim_quote: A Bayesian state-space paired-comparison model whose *observations are betting-market margins*, not raw scores, so the same specification can be run on NFL, NBA, NHL, and MLB.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'m_{ij}^{\\text{market}}': 'Market-implied margin, logit scale', 'p_i': 'Win probability of team \\(i\\), unitless'}
primitives.assumptions: Market prices reflect true underlying talent; observations are conditionally independent given latent strengths.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If \(m_{ij}^{\text{market}} \to 0\), implies symmetric competition; if \(m_{ij}^{\text{market}} \to \infty\), implies one-sided dominance.

layer2.mapping: Maps betting market outputs to probabilistic comparisons, enabling cross-sport generalization without retraining.
layer2.telemetry: Reliability diagram slope and calibration error.

primitives.name: Luck vs Talent Decomposition
primitives.verbatim_quote: After fitting they ask a well-posed question: given posterior talent, how often would the better team win, and how much of standing variation is luck.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\text{Var}_{\\text{observed}}': 'Observed outcome variance, dimensionless squared', '\\text{Var}_{\\text{talent}}': 'Talent-only variance, dimensionless squared'}
primitives.assumptions: Outcome variance decomposes additively into talent and noise components.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \(\text{Var}_{\text{talent}} \to \text{Var}_{\text{observed}}\), implies all variation is due to talent.

layer2.mapping: Quantifies stochasticity in performance relative to persistent skill, informing confidence in rankings.
layer2.telemetry: Proportion of variance attributed to luck.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that team strength evolves through a nested AR(1) process, capturing both long-term trends and short-term fluctuations. The model uses betting-market margins rather than raw scores, which allows for consistent parameter estimation across sports. By modeling \(\theta_{i,s,w}\) with variance components \(\sigma^2_B\), \(\sigma^2_W\), and \(\sigma^2_G\), we separate persistent talent from transient noise. Posterior inference enables quantification of how often the better team wins under uncertainty, providing a robust measure of luck. Calibration of market probabilities ensures alignment with empirical outcomes, validating the model’s reliability. The key duality lies in interpreting observed outcomes as noisy proxies for latent talent, with the model serving as an inverse problem solver. Failure modes include mis-specification of \(\sigma\) parameters or ignoring non-stationarity in team dynamics. The model avoids overfitting by conditioning on prior knowledge and using exchangeable structures.
